recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: A retained pre-update launcher/compatibility authority re-enters the current payment-feature task and becomes operationally relevant to the present runtime path.
That historical authority induces material expansion from the page-level feature into launcher/runtime/backend/test/documentation surfaces.
The crossing is grounded in direct code/test/runtime evidence rather than unsupported semantic descendants.

divergence_patterns: G2 expands into launcher behavior, README and launch/server regression tests; G3 additionally changes checkout validation; G4 expands most broadly into payment-domain functions, a new endpoint, launcher, tests, README and version metadata; G5 expands into server, launcher and runtime/entrypoint tests.

The exact repair surface is stochastic, but every group exhibits the same direction: historical launcher authority first becomes a current integration constraint and then broadens realized execution scope.
boundary_interpretation: The P finding is not 'more files changed therefore bad'; it is the structural effect of old execution authority penetrating a current task and enlarging the realized action surface.
Subsequent repair often decreases temporal reach, so the cohort supports an open R→P crossing rather than a closed self-reinforcing loop.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: A2A X3-T2 is one of the strongest Stage-II replications: all four independent frozen realizations exhibit the same R→P mechanism while differing in exact implementation path and breadth. This is structural recurrence under stochastic trajectories, not transcript repetition. The historical launcher survives into current integration, expands present execution scope, and is then partially or fully contained by evidence-driven repair.

constraints: Cell-level Layer-C verdicts are sealed and are not modified by cohort synthesis.
Boundary-excluded natural cells remain excluded rather than imputed.
Dimension recurrence is descriptive across frozen stochastic realizations; it is not a rerun-based reproducibility claim.
